about.tool: A broad-edged pen held fairly flat, at about 30° (the sheet: nearly parallel to the line, up to 30°).
about.proportions: x-height 4 nib widths; ascenders and descenders short, about a third of the x-height; capitals 5 1/2 nib widths.
about.features: Rotunda: a round, open, lighter blackletter: wide round bowls broken only slightly at the top and bottom, stems cut square, short extenders, the Rotunda a with its curl and diamond bowl, the upright d, a wide round s with a diamond on its spine; capitals wide, with a lead-in tick, doubled stems and a diagonal hairline. The 2-shaped r (after round letters) and the long s are not part of the a-z here; the capitals' paired hairlines are written as one.
about.history: The gothic book hand of Italy and Spain, 13th to 15th centuries (Bologna's law books, the great choir books), rounder than the northern Textura; the model of the first Italian gothic types.
